consensus_summary: Wheat primarily symbolizes God’s righteous people or true believers—the children of the kingdom—who are gathered and saved at the final judgment.
book_summary: Wheat is identified as the children of the kingdom, depicted as good grain gathered into the barn at harvest.
consensus_core_identification: Wheat = the children of God’s kingdom, gathered at the final harvest.
book_core_identification: Wheat/good grain = the children of the kingdom, gathered into the barn at harvest.
boundary_disagreement: None material. The consensus mentions broader synonymous labels such as “righteous,” “true believers,” and “elect,” while the book uses the explicit Matthean phrase “children of the kingdom.” This is wording and scriptural precision, not a changed boundary.
rationale: The book states exactly the dominant identification reported by the blind consensus and preserves the same harvest-and-gathering context. Its concise wording omits the consensus’s secondary symbolic uses of wheat, but an entry’s focus on the primary meaning does not reject or reclassify those context-dependent alternatives.
strongest_objection: Matthew 13:38 literally identifies the “good seed,” rather than the mature wheat by name, as the children of the kingdom. Even so, the parable’s crop imagery and Matthew 3:12’s explicit wheat gathered into the garner strongly support the entry’s combined identification.
